title: Compare upstream menu miss guard with fork fallback
platforms: Linux interpreter and desktop source; GUI untested
changes: Compare the upstream desktop background-confirm guard against a recognized action-menu miss modeled through the fork core.
validation: For an in-view point rejected by the fork Actions layout at frame 40, the modeled fork fallback queued A; the upstream guard expression disallowed A for a recognized menu. Control and click states diverged and ROM/snapshot hashes remained unchanged.
limitations: No window event or upstream runtime was exercised; the guard does not by itself prove protection during a partial reveal without a recognized menu. Isolated build emitted seven unused-code warnings.
The managed cleanup helper rejected the U31 unit because it accepts only target/rom-data-*; evidence is retained.
